slides.title: Heap Allocation Mechanics
slides.prompt: 'new' allocates memory on the Heap. 'delete' deallocates single items, and 'delete[]' deallocates dynamic arrays to prevent memory leaks.

slides.title: Dynamic Allocation Operator
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword to dynamically allocate a single integer on heap.

slides.title: Deallocating Dynamic Memory
slides.prompt: What is the proper way to free memory allocated with 'new int[100]'?

slides.title: Array Dynamic Allocation
slides.prompt: Fill in the operator to allocate dynamic array of 5 elements.

slides.title: Memory Allocation Failure
slides.prompt: What exception is thrown when 'new' fails to allocate requested memory?

slides.title: Nothrow Variant for new
slides.prompt: Fill in constant argument used to return nullptr instead of throwing on allocation failure.

slides.title: Stack vs Heap Lifetime
slides.prompt: How long does dynamic memory allocated with 'new' persist in memory?
options: Until explicitly freed with delete/delete[] or the program terminates
Until the enclosing function scope finishes execution
For a fixed duration of 10 seconds
slides.correctAnswer: Until explicitly freed with delete/delete[] or the program terminates

slides.title: Dynamic Initialization Syntax
slides.prompt: Fill in syntax to allocate and initialize dynamic double value to 3.14.

slides.title: Mismatching delete and new[]
slides.prompt: What happens if you use 'delete ptr' instead of 'delete[] ptr' for an array allocated with 'new T[N]'?
options: Undefined behavior (destructors for remaining elements are not called)
The compiler automatically corrects it to delete[]
Only the last element is deleted
slides.correctAnswer: Undefined behavior (destructors for remaining elements are not called)
